prompt: Assess this claim: black people have been denied voting rights because of race.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is historically accurate. In the United States, Black people were explicitly denied voting rights because of race through laws restricting voting to white people.

The Fifteenth Amendment, ratified in 1870, prohibited racial discrimination in voting, but many states subsequently used literacy tests, poll taxes, discriminatory registration practices, and intimidation to disenfranchise Black voters. Some measures were race-neutral in wording but deliberately designed or administered to exclude Black people. The Voting Rights Act of 1965 targeted these practices.

The claim also applies elsewhere—for example, apartheid South Africa excluded Black people from the national franchise. It does not mean every Black person, everywhere, has always been denied voting rights.
